newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela aluminum cos lose over $36 mln/yr - govt.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela aluminum cos lose over $36 mln/yr - govt.

text.p: Aluminum companies in Venezuelan state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana (CVG), due to be privatized later this year, are losing over $36 million a year, a government minister said.

"Their cash flow is about $198 million per year and they need about $234 million to keep going," Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) president Alberto Poletto, whose portfolio includes privatization, told Reuters in an exclusive interview.
"If you include their needed environmental upgrade, their cost to the government -- if they are not sold -- would be about $500 million over the next few year," Poletto said.
Much of the losses are due to high service payments on $1.2 billion of debt, Poletto said.

Thirteen companies have qualified to bid for CVG's four aluminum companies -- smelters Venalum and Alcasa, bauxite producer Bauxilum and carbon anode producer Carbonorca -- including: Alcoa, Gencor, Alumax, Reynolds Metals Co, Norsk Hydro ASA and RTZ Corp.
